title: PRAYING GOD'S OWN WORDS BACK TO HIM

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But Moses sought the favour of the Lord his God. 'Lord,' he said, 'why should your anger burn against your people, whom you brought out of Egypt with great power and a mighty hand? Why should the Egyptians say, "It was with evil intent that he brought them out, to kill them in the mountains and to wipe them off the face of the earth"? Turn from your fierce anger; relent and do not bring disaster on your people.'" - Exod 32:11-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Look closely at how Moses prays. He does not defend Israel. He cannot — there is no defence. Instead he appeals to God's own purposes and God's own reputation.

Notice the quiet correction: God had said "your people, whom you brought up." Moses replies, "your people, whom you brought out of Egypt with great power." Moses gently hands them back to God. He knows he never rescued anyone. God did.

This is a model for our praying. When we have nothing good to plead about ourselves, we can plead who God is and what He has already done. Moses is not manipulating God; he is agreeing with God. He is asking God to act in a way consistent with everything God has revealed about Himself.

And Moses cares about God's name among the nations. His concern is not merely "save my friends" but "let Your glory not be slandered." That is a mature prayer.

Every believer can pray this way through Christ. We do not come with our record; we come in His name (John 14:13-14). The strongest prayer you can pray is one that asks God to be true to Himself.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When you pray, do you appeal more to your worthiness or to God's character?
2. Are you concerned about God's reputation, or only your own comfort?
3. What promise of God could you pray back to Him today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, when I have no case to make for myself, I plead Your mercy and Your name. Act for Your glory, Lord. Amen.
